summary: Multipath handoff triggers session micro-redirects and intermittent inference stalls for customer
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightData Analytics reported intermittent long-tail latency and streaming cancellations for inference requests originating from their us-west region. Symptoms began ~2026-03-09 21:00 UTC and recurred in short bursts; streaming sessions either delayed p99 > 10s or aborted with client-side cancel after 20s. Impact: user-facing timeouts for their product and elevated error rate on their pipeline.

Impact:
- Several customer endpoints showed p95/p99 latency regressions and increased 504s on streaming connections.
- A subset of requests were observed to flip egress paths mid-session (us-west -> eu-west) causing re-handshakes and KV-cache misses.

Environment:
- Customer uses Dedicated capacity in us-west with cross-region fallback to eu-west.
- Traffic pattern: bursty inference streams during their batch scoring windows.
- Observed model: gpt-redwood-13b-v1 pinned in customer config.

Observed at time of report:
- First alert at 2026-03-09 20:58 UTC from customer. Support ticket opened 2026-03-10 01:12 local (report time converted).

Primary hypothesis in initial report:
- Intermediate multipath handoff at an egress-pop caused session micro-redirects, forcing repeated TLS handshakes and KV cache invalidation which increased tail latency and aborted streams.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer issues streaming chat requests to api.redwood.example/v1/stream with region=us-west header
2) Generate burst load to simulate scheduled scoring (150-300 rps for 30s bursts),
3) Observe p50/p95/p99 in Console route dashboard and streaming disconnect rate
4) Correlate request IDs in edge-proxy logs with downstream pop and egress path changes
logs: sample_request_id=brd-req-20260309-11a4f2 - initial TLS handshake at pop-usw-1 -> forwarded to pop-euw-3 after 1.2s: 'egress_route_change=true'
edge-proxy.log snippet: [2026-03-09T20:59:03Z] session=brd-req-20260309-11a4f2 action=reroute reason=multipath_handoff path_before=POP-USW-1 path_after=POP-EUW-3 ttl_delta=+3s
serving-runtime trace: request_id=brd-req-20260309-11a4f2 stage=kv_cache_miss cause=remote_node_swap latency_tokens=370ms total_infer=12.4s
comments: 2026-03-10 01:20 - Support (Asha): Received initial report from customer. Collected request IDs and asked for sample logs and time ranges. Escalating to SRE for routing analysis.

2026-03-10 03:05 - SRE (Miguel): Observed multipath handoffs in flow logs between POP-USW-1 and POP-EUW-3 coincident with latency spikes. TTLs show additional handshake time when path flips. Hypothesis: route score recalculation caused by transient bgp/peer latency spike at 20:59 UTC.

2026-03-10 08:58 - Customer (BrightData - Emma Li): Provided traffic window and confirmed they pin a model but use cross-region fallback. Noted that issue frequency correlates to their 21:00 PST batch runs.
2026-03-10 11:40 - Support (Asha): Applied temporary account-level routing override to enforce pop-affinity to POP-USW-1 for BrightData while investigation continues.
2026-03-11 02:10 - SRE (Miguel): Deployed edge-proxy fix (preserve-upstream-stickiness on multipath detection) to canary in us-west. Monitoring for recurrence.
2026-03-12 09:00 - Support (Asha): Customer confirmed mitigation removed errors and p99 returned to baseline. Closing incident and documenting mitigation steps.
investigation_notes: Correlation of trace IDs shows reroutes occur within 500-1500ms windows after initial egress selection under bursty load.
BGP and peering graphs show a transient latency increase on peering link to pop-usw-1 at 20:58-21:04 UTC causing route-score adjustments from the route-agent service.
Edge-proxy currently treats multipath detection as a soft signal and may issue mid-session reroutes; this allowed a small fraction (~0.6%) of sessions to be handed off during high burst windows.
KV cache invalidations were observed when serving-runtime saw backend host swap; this amplified token generation latency by up to 10-12s on affected sessions.
No evidence of model-serving GPU degradation or Dedicated pool saturation during windows — metrics stable for GPU utilization and queue lengths.
Reproduction in staging: simulated peering latency > 180ms triggered same mid-session handoff behavior and streaming aborts.
Mitigation validated: account-level pop affinity + edge-proxy sticky fix reduced handoffs to <0.01% in canary traffic and removed the long-tail latency spikes for the customer.
resolution:
Root cause: transient peering latency increased route-agent score variance which caused the edge-proxy to trigger multipath handoffs mid-session. Those handoffs forced TLS re-handshakes and KV cache misses in the serving-runtime, producing long-tail inference latency and streaming cancellations.

Fix and rollout summary:
- Immediate workaround: applied customer-level pop-affinity to lock BrightData to POP-USW-1 for their scheduled batch window.
- Short-term fix: deployed edge-proxy patch to preserve upstream stickiness when multipath signals are noisy (canary -> us-west -> global rollout complete 2026-03-11).
- Follow-up actions: create a route-agent improvement to debounce route-score adjustments under short-lived peering jitter, update runbook, and notify network partners about peering stability window.

Customer status: BrightData confirmed restored performance and requested post-incident notes. Incident closed after monitoring 48 hours with no recurrence.
